_about: Round 143: a personal story for each Wayfarer -- three chapters that open as trust grows (20, 45, 70). Each asks one thing (items, fights, a floor, crafts, sitting still, gathering) and pays a little insight, gold or pills -- and makes their gift 8% stronger while they travel with you (24% after the third). Scripts: scripts/systems/WayfarerStories.gd.

Marin Ashgrove.title: Counting Bandages
Marin Ashgrove.ask: "I keep counting bandages I don't have. Bring me three healing salves and I'll stop pretending torn shirts will do."
Marin Ashgrove.done: She counts them twice, then laughs at herself. "Three. Good. Now I can think about something else for a minute."

Marin Ashgrove.title: The War Nobody Remembers
Marin Ashgrove.ask: "I never told anyone why I walked out. Come down with me to floor 5 -- I want to stand somewhere the dead aren't mine."
Marin Ashgrove.done: She stands very still at the bottom, and then she tells you all of it. It takes a long time. You don't interrupt. "Thank you for the quiet," she says.

Marin Ashgrove.title: Needed for Something Else
Marin Ashgrove.ask: "I'd like to be needed for something that isn't a wound. Teach me. Brew five medicines with me watching -- the kind that stop things hurting before they start."
Marin Ashgrove.done: She holds the last bottle to the light. "Thirty years of bandages. Tonight I made tea for a stranger and it was the best thing I've done."

Dorn Quill.title: A Quiet Pair of Eyes
Dorn Quill.ask: "I walk behind. I'd like to see how you move before I decide how to walk. Win fifteen fights while I watch."
Dorn Quill.done: He nods once. "You favour your left. Fix it. Otherwise -- good. I've walked behind worse."

Dorn Quill.title: What the Fire Left
Dorn Quill.ask: "The valley I came from burned. Nothing there will ever grow back the same. Bring me six spirit herbs -- I'd like to put something green in a pot."
Dorn Quill.done: He plants them in an old tin cup and sets it where the sun will find it. "It won't live," he says. He checks it every hour anyway.

Dorn Quill.title: Ground That Isn't Burned
Dorn Quill.ask: "Show me a place the fire hasn't touched. Floor 8. I want to read its tracks."
Dorn Quill.done: He kneels in the dust a long time, then looks up. "It's still there. Under all of it, the world is still there. I forgot."

Hesk the Younger.title: The Line I Practised
Hesk the Younger.ask: "I need to see you fight, if I'm going to stand in front of you. Twenty fights. I'll be right here. Pretending I'm not nervous."
Hesk the Younger.done: He lets out a breath he's been holding since the village. "You don't need protecting. That's a relief. And a little insulting."

Hesk the Younger.title: My Father's Shield
Hesk the Younger.ask: "The rim is cracked and I can't afford to mend it. Eight iron ore, and I'll finally be able to look at it without my hands shaking."
Hesk the Younger.done: He works the rim until dark and does not speak. When he hands you the shield to hold, it is heavier than it looks. "It's balanced now. He'd have liked that."

Hesk the Younger.title: Someone to Stand In Front Of
Hesk the Younger.ask: "I want to be at the front when it counts. Take me to floor 12. Let me find out if I'm the thing he said I'd be."
Hesk the Younger.done: He doesn't drop the shield. Not once. At the bottom he sits down hard and laughs until he cries. "I held the line," he says. "Did you see? I held it."

Tamsin Reed.title: The Crow Is Hungry
Tamsin Reed.ask: "The crow isn't mine and it's decided I owe it fish. Three cave carp, and I promise it will stop looking at me like that."
Tamsin Reed.done: The crow takes the fish, looks at you for a long moment, and then -- very deliberately -- sits on your shoulder instead of hers. "Well," she says. "That's a verdict."

Tamsin Reed.title: Sit With Me
Tamsin Reed.ask: "Animals come to the ones who stay still. Sit with me five minutes. You'll feel stupid. Then you won't."
Tamsin Reed.hint: sit with her for five minutes
Tamsin Reed.done: Something small and brown has curled up beside your knee. Neither of you moves for a long time. "See?" she whispers. "They don't ask what you're for."

Tamsin Reed.title: Every Beast Chose Its Person
Tamsin Reed.ask: "I think the deep has more creatures like the hare than anyone knows. Take me to floor 12 and let me listen."
Tamsin Reed.done: She stands in the dark with her eyes closed, smiling. "They're all singing," she says. "Every one. Did you hear it? They're all so glad someone came."

Lio Verrane.title: Eleven Duels
Lio Verrane.ask: "Let me watch you for a bit. Twenty-five fights. I'll learn something. I always do. It's a terrible habit, being gracious."
Lio Verrane.done: He applauds, once, loudly. "The third one -- the lunge. I'm stealing it. I'll tell everyone I invented it."

Lio Verrane.title: A Blade Worth Losing To
Lio Verrane.ask: "A duellist is only as good as his steel, and mine is embarrassing. Make three smithing pieces and let me hold them. I'll tell you which one would have beaten me."
Lio Verrane.done: He tests each against his own, frowning. At the last one he grins. "That one. That one would have beaten me. I'm so pleased I could cry."

Lio Verrane.title: The Twelfth
Lio Verrane.ask: "Take me down to floor 18. If I'm ever going to fight the twelfth, I'd rather it be somewhere worth the flourish."
Lio Verrane.done: He bows to the dark itself, an honest flourish this time, no pretending. "Thank you," he says, to the room. "I lost beautifully."

Sister Wen.title: Sit Like Someone Listening
Sister Wen.ask: "Sit ten minutes. Don't try to get anywhere. I'll be next to you. Pretend I'm a stone."
Sister Wen.hint: sit for ten minutes with her
Sister Wen.done: "Mm. You almost stopped, just at the end. Almost. That's the hardest part, and you reached it on the first try. I'm annoyed."

Sister Wen.title: Tea and Argument
Sister Wen.ask: "Three moonpetals. I'd like to make tea, and I would like you to tell me, over it, why you think the deep is the way it is. Argue with me. I mean it."
Sister Wen.done: The tea is bitter and the argument runs past midnight. "You were wrong about two things and right about one," she says. "I've decided the one matters."

Sister Wen.title: The Long Stillness
Sister Wen.ask: "Twenty minutes. Not trying. I want to see what happens when someone I trust stops being afraid of the quiet."
Sister Wen.hint: sit for twenty minutes with her
Sister Wen.done: When you open your eyes she is crying, and smiling, and does not explain. "Thank you," she says. "My teachers never once asked me to stay."

Brask Orren.title: Iron Worth Hitting
Brask Orren.ask: "I've no ore, no coal and a very bad temper. Ten iron ore, and I'll light the anvil on my back for the first time in a month."
Brask Orren.done: The anvil rings for an hour. "Hear that? That's iron that wants to be something. Nothing in the world sounds better."

Brask Orren.title: Prove It on the Anvil
Brask Orren.ask: "Words are cheap. Make five smithing pieces with me heckling you. If any of them are crooked I'll say so, loudly."
Brask Orren.done: He goes quiet over the last one -- the longest silence you've ever heard from him. "Straight," he says at last. "Straight as a rule. I haven't a single complaint. I'm furious."

Brask Orren.title: Why the Anvil
Brask Orren.ask: "I'll tell you why I carry it, if you make me eight more things worth hammering. Eight, and no shortcuts."
Brask Orren.done: "It was my master's. He died at the bench. I carry it so he can keep working." He taps the anvil. "Yes, I know how that sounds. Hold it for a moment." The iron is warm.

Vey Calder.title: A Debt, Not a Price
Vey Calder.ask: "Sixty gold, for a debt I'm settling. I won't ask you to trust me with it. I'll just see that it comes back, in ways you won't be able to count."
Vey Calder.done: He folds the coins away without counting them. "You didn't ask what it was for. Do you know how rare that is? You've just become the best-liked person in this pagoda."

Vey Calder.title: Everyone Owes Someone
Vey Calder.ask: "Take me down to floor 20 and I'll show you how the deep keeps its books. Everything that lives down there owes something to something else."
Vey Calder.done: He walks a slow circle and names, softly, every debt in the room. "None of it is mine," he says, surprised. "For the first time, none of it is mine."

Vey Calder.title: Owing Someone
Vey Calder.ask: "Sixty fights. I want to see what you're like when you're owed nothing and give it anyway."
Vey Calder.done: He is quiet for a long moment. "I used to keep a ledger of favours," he says. "I've stopped. I didn't see the point of keeping count of you."

Pell Ardent.title: It Hums in a Lovely Key
Pell Ardent.ask: "Sit -- sorry, could you sit? Eight minutes. I just want to listen to it hum. I won't touch. I'll touch a little. Sit, please!"
Pell Ardent.done: She is scribbling before you open your eyes. "It's a minor sixth! A minor sixth! I'm sorry, I'm sorry, I'll explain -- no, you don't need me to -- it's so beautiful."

Pell Ardent.title: Three Little Shards
Pell Ardent.ask: "I need three nanite shards to build something. I can't explain it without finishing the sentence and I keep not finishing the sentence. Three shards?"
Pell Ardent.done: She builds a tiny brass bell that rings in exactly the key of your swarm, and she gives it to the air instead of you. "Sorry," she says. "It wanted to be freed. Not given. Freed."

Pell Ardent.title: Where It Goes
Pell Ardent.ask: "Floor 30. I'd like to see where it goes -- your swarm. I think it wants to go there. I think it's been trying to tell me."
Pell Ardent.done: She doesn't speak for a long time -- the longest in her life. Then: "It's not tuning. It was never tuning. It was... saying hello." She is trembling, and laughing, and utterly sure.

Isolde Kern.title: Forty-One Paces
Isolde Kern.ask: "Thirty fights. I record them. Not to judge -- to learn the wind. You'd be surprised how much a person's style changes the air."
Isolde Kern.done: She closes her notebook. "Wind from the left, always. You turn into it. Good habit. I've written you down."

Isolde Kern.title: Fletching
Isolde Kern.ask: "Five bone shards. I make my own. It's a nervous habit and also, I promise, a precise one."
Isolde Kern.done: She fletches them in silence and hands you one, flight true as a ruler. "For when you're alone," she says. "Not that you will be." She does not look at you when she says it.

Isolde Kern.title: Where to Stand
Isolde Kern.ask: "Floor 40. You've never once told me where to stand. I'd like to choose to stand beside you there, if you'll have me."
Isolde Kern.done: She sets down the rifle -- the first time you've seen it out of her hands. "I have never missed since the day I decided," she says. "I decided something else today. Mark it."

Odalys Wren.title: Rue and Nettle
Odalys Wren.ask: "The nettles are restless and I'm out of leaf. Bring me four spirit herbs and I'll tell you what they were so upset about."
Odalys Wren.done: She sniffs each herb, nods, and mutters to them like old friends. "Fresh. Good. They say you have a kind face. They are not reliable."

Odalys Wren.title: The Hedge Remembers
Odalys Wren.ask: "I have not been past the fifth floor since I lost my teacher. Walk me down. I want to ask the old roots a question."
Odalys Wren.done: She kneels at the bottom and presses her palm to the stone for a long time. "Still there," she says, and does not explain.

Odalys Wren.title: Cures She Believes In
Odalys Wren.ask: "Sit with me while I brew. Five medicines, start to finish, and no charms. I want to prove I can do it without lying to anyone."
Odalys Wren.done: She stoppers the last bottle and holds it up to the light. "No charm in it. Just the cure." She is laughing, and a little tearful.

Tobiah Reeve.title: A Quiet Road
Tobiah Reeve.ask: "Quiet road is a lying road. Let me watch you work. Put down fifteen of whatever's out there and I'll know if you're worth guarding."
Tobiah Reeve.done: He leans on a wall, arms folded, and has not blinked once. "Hm. You check your corners. Most never learn."

Tobiah Reeve.title: Tea for the Door
Tobiah Reeve.ask: "Thirty years I sat with my back to the wall. A man needs a proper cup after that. Bring six spirit herbs and I'll steep us something fine."
Tobiah Reeve.done: The tea is dreadful and he is delighted with it. "Best cup I've had since the caravans. Don't tell the cook."

Tobiah Reeve.title: The Last Wagon
Tobiah Reeve.ask: "My last wagon went down on the eighth floor and I never went back to see. I'd like to, with someone I trust at the door."
Tobiah Reeve.done: He finds the splintered axle, and touches it once. "Good wood. Poor luck." He stands a while, then turns his back to the wall for the first time and does not mind.

Zhu Ling.title: A Steady Hand
Zhu Ling.ask: "A scribe can only copy what holds still. Sit with me five minutes, quiet, so I can sketch your stillness. It is harder than you think."
Zhu Ling.done: She finishes the sketch, frowns, and shows you. It is surprisingly kind. "You fidget with your hands. Everyone does. Everyone should."

Zhu Ling.title: Ink and Silver
Zhu Ling.ask: "My ink runs out in the damp. Bring me three moonpetals and I will make you something that does not fade."
Zhu Ling.done: She grinds the petals into a pale ink and writes a single line on your sleeve. "There. Read it when you need to." You cannot read it. It helps anyway.

Zhu Ling.title: The Wall I Want
Zhu Ling.ask: "There is a wall on the twelfth floor no scribe has copied. I would very much like to be the first, with you holding the lantern."
Zhu Ling.done: She copies for hours and does not say a word. At the end she signs her name in the corner. "First," she whispers. "And you were there."

Kell Varga.title: Opening the Ledger
Kell Varga.ask: "Everyone owes something. Prove yours is worth collecting. Twenty kills, clean, and I'll start a line in your name."
Kell Varga.done: He writes a number in a notebook that looks very old. "That's the first. Don't make me regret the second."

Kell Varga.title: Debts of Iron
Kell Varga.ask: "The guild paid in iron, once. Bring me eight iron ore and I'll settle an old account out of my own pocket."
Kell Varga.done: He weighs the ore in his hand and nods. "Settled. First debt I've paid in years. Feels strange."

Kell Varga.title: No Debts Between Us
Kell Varga.ask: "I want to go where the guild's last collection was due. Floor twelve. I'd like to see it finished."
Kell Varga.done: He finds the empty room, looks at it, and tears a page out of the ledger. "Closed." He gives you the blank page. "For luck."

Neve Aldous.title: Patience
Neve Aldous.ask: "You can't hurry a catch. Sit with me ten minutes without speaking, and we'll see if the water likes you."
Neve Aldous.done: She says nothing for a while longer, then nods once. "It likes you. That's unusual. I don't trust that."

Neve Aldous.title: Bait
Neve Aldous.ask: "Cave carp go for moonpetal, everyone forgets that. Bring me three and I'll catch you something worth the walk."
Neve Aldous.done: She cuts the line with a steady hand, and an hour later holds up a silver fish no larger than her palm. "Dinner. And a good omen."

Neve Aldous.title: The Deep Water
Neve Aldous.ask: "There is a lake on the eighteenth floor that doesn't freeze. I'd like to see it once before I stop being able to."
Neve Aldous.done: She casts a line into black water and sits for a very long time. Nothing bites. She smiles anyway. "Perfect."

Rhosyn Dale.title: A Warm-Up
Rhosyn Dale.ask: "I need a crowd. Failing that, I need targets. Put down twenty-five of the things that don't deserve applause."
Rhosyn Dale.done: She spits a thin ribbon of flame and takes a bow to nobody. "Not bad! You don't flinch. I like that."

Rhosyn Dale.title: Fuel
Rhosyn Dale.ask: "Good fire needs good iron to hold it. Forge three things with me watching, and I'll show you a trick that isn't a trick."
Rhosyn Dale.done: She holds a spark in her palm and lets you feel the heat. "That's mine. It's been mine the whole time."

Rhosyn Dale.title: The Big Finish
Rhosyn Dale.ask: "I'd like to do one show for people who aren't paying. Take me down to the eighteenth floor and I'll light the whole place up."
Rhosyn Dale.done: She spreads her arms and the cavern fills with warm gold light. She is crying and grinning at once. "Best crowd I ever had. All three of you."

Anselm Thorne.title: The Count
Anselm Thorne.ask: "I hear the hour in everything. Let me hear yours. Sit with me eight minutes and breathe slowly."
Anselm Thorne.done: He taps a very slow beat on his knee, matching your breath. "Steady. You'll do. Not many do."

Anselm Thorne.title: Bell Metal
Anselm Thorne.ask: "A bell needs good iron and patience. Bring me ten iron ore and I will tell you how a town sounds when it is happy."
Anselm Thorne.done: He turns the ore over, weighs it, and hums a single low note. "Right. That's the note. That's what I miss."

Anselm Thorne.title: The Drowned Tower
Anselm Thorne.ask: "The tower went under on floor fifteen's tide. I want to ring something there, just once, before I leave it."
Anselm Thorne.done: He strikes a rock with an iron rod. The sound goes on and on. When it fades, he bows his head. "Thank you for the company."

Saffi Okoro.title: Samples
Saffi Okoro.ask: "I never trade blind. Bring me five spirit herbs so I know what grows near you, and I'll tell you what grows in my pockets."
Saffi Okoro.done: She tastes a leaf, nods, and hides three seeds in your pack when you aren't looking. "Free sample. Don't tell."

Saffi Okoro.title: A Fair Price
Saffi Okoro.ask: "I've overcharged half the world. Make five medicines honestly and I'll sell you one thing at the true price. Once."
Saffi Okoro.done: She sets a seed on your palm and names a price. It is, shockingly, fair. "Don't get used to it."

Saffi Okoro.title: Banned Gardens
Saffi Okoro.ask: "There's a place on floor twenty where plants grow that nobody's allowed to. Come help me plant there. Just a handful."
Saffi Okoro.done: She plants a dozen seeds in cracked soil, watering them with her own canteen. "Come back in a year," she says. "If we're alive, they will be."

Barrow Quill.title: Company
Barrow Quill.ask: "The dead keep quiet and the living talk too much. Sit a while, ten minutes, and tell me nothing."
Barrow Quill.done: He lets the silence run well past ten minutes, then sighs. "Good. Most people can't. You can."

Barrow Quill.title: Marking Stones
Barrow Quill.ask: "I mark each one with a bone. Bring me five bone shards, and I'll leave a mark for anyone who didn't get one."
Barrow Quill.done: He sets the shards one by one, whispering a name for each. "That's them seen. That's all they wanted."

Barrow Quill.title: Keeping the Living
Barrow Quill.ask: "I've never gone below the twentieth floor. The dead there are lonelier. Come down with me, and keep the living company too."
Barrow Quill.done: He walks the corridors for an hour, nodding to the walls. At the end he laughs for the first time you have heard. "They liked you."

Ysolde Kane.title: A Test Shot
Ysolde Kane.ask: "I only follow what I can't out-shoot. Prove you can keep pace. Thirty kills, no dawdling."
Ysolde Kane.done: She stops counting at twenty-six and pretends she meant to. "Fine. You're quick. Not quicker than me."

Ysolde Kane.title: Fletching
Ysolde Kane.ask: "Good feathers are hard to come by. Bring me five bone shards for the heads, and I'll make arrows that do not miss."
Ysolde Kane.done: She fletches a shaft in front of you, careful and quick. "There. Aim true." She grins.

Ysolde Kane.title: The Last Message
Ysolde Kane.ask: "I carried one message I never delivered. It was meant for the thirtieth floor. Walk with me, and I'll finally let it go."
Ysolde Kane.done: She fires her last arrow into the dark and listens. "Delivered," she says. For the first time, she doesn't count where it lands.

Momo Ha.title: Still Water
Momo Ha.ask: "The tea spirit says the first cup is for listening. Sit with me five minutes and listen."
Momo Ha.done: She pours nothing into two cups and hands you one. "See? Warm." You can honestly feel the warmth.

Momo Ha.title: Leaves of the Moon
Momo Ha.ask: "The best brews need moonpetal. Bring me three and I'll steep something the spirit will actually drink."
Momo Ha.done: She steeps them in silence, and the air smells faintly of rain on warm stone. "It drank it. It never drinks."

Momo Ha.title: The Spirit's Garden
Momo Ha.ask: "The spirit says there's a garden on floor forty. It wants to go home. Walk us there?"
Momo Ha.done: The air shivers and a small warm presence settles briefly on your shoulder. Momo bows deeply. "It says thank you. It says you can keep the cup."
